title: Second Law of Motion
theory:
**Big idea:** Force causes acceleration. The bigger the force, the bigger the acceleration, and the bigger the mass, the smaller the acceleration.

**Newton's second law**
Measured from an **inertial frame**, a particle's acceleration equals the **vector sum of all forces** on it divided by its mass:
**a = F/m, or F = ma**

**Key points**
- **a** is in the **same direction** as the net force **F**.
- **F** and **a** are taken at the **same instant**. If the force stops, the acceleration becomes zero at that very instant (the velocity stays at whatever it had reached).
- **Unit:** 1 N = 1 kg × 1 m/s² = 1 kg m/s².
- The first law is a special case: if F = 0, then a = 0.

**🧮 Worked examples**
- A 10 N net force on a 2 kg body gives a = 10/2 = **5 m/s²**.
- To give a 1000 kg car an acceleration of 2 m/s², you need F = 1000 × 2 = **2000 N**.
- The same force on double the mass gives **half** the acceleration.

> ⚠️ **Common mistake:** Using just one force in F = ma. F is the **net** (vector sum) force from everything acting on the body.

questions.prompt: Newton's second law, written for an inertial frame, is:
A net force of 10 N acts on a body of mass 2 kg. Its acceleration is:
The direction of the acceleration of a particle is always the same as the direction of:

options.text: The largest single force on it

questions.explanation: a = **F**/m, so **a** points along the net force (not necessarily along the velocity).

questions.prompt: The force acting on a moving particle suddenly becomes zero. At that instant, its acceleration:

options.text: Stays the same for a while

questions.explanation: F and a are related at the same instant, so no force means no acceleration.

questions.prompt: What net force is needed to give a 1000 kg car an acceleration of 2 m/s²?
The same net force acts on two bodies, one of which has twice the mass of the other. The heavier body's acceleration is:

options.text: Twice that of the lighter body
Half that of the lighter body
Equal to that of the lighter body
Four times that of the lighter body

questions.explanation: a = F/m, so doubling m halves a.
